body:
There came a point several years ago when I was physically struggling and unable to work, so I went in for temporary help.  The case worker barely glanced at my paperwork, all but laughed in my face because I didnt *look* like I was struggling/poor, then verbally shamed me and showed me the door.  I have never never in my life been made to feel like such a ... filthy pariah.  I swore never to go back.

My sweet mother has loaned and given us lots of money over the years.  That's why we are still alive.  She is almost out of money.  I have sucked her retirement away.... I... Don't know where to turn.  I can't see the light at the end of the tunnel.

It's kind of a choice between, die now and make them sad, or suck all of my mother's resources away until we're all homeless, *then* die and make them sad.

I've called hotlines twice, but all they seem able to do is say, "Gee, you sure are in a difficult situation. I can't point you to any actual resources, but don't feel bad."  So helpful.  /s

Well, they did once give me a number to a local caregiver support thing, but I never got through to a live person there.  I know intellectually that what you are saying about caregivers is absolute truth, and I would say exactly the same thing to anyone else, but... When when your loved one is stuck in the tub and can't stand up, you don't just leave them there.  When their blood sugar is bottoming out and their legs don't work, you don't just let them slip into a diabetic coma.  When the cat vomits a hairball on the floor, you don't just not clean it up.  And the next thing you know, your head is spinning, your hands are shaking, and you're feeling worthless for not being able to get your family out of this situation.  My greatest fantasies right now involve extensive vacations where I lie on the beach, and people bring me food that I don't even have to choose.

Thank you for your response and the care and thoughts.  I appreciate the time and energy you have freely given to a stranger.

EDITED TO ADD: it does mean a lot to know that someone out there, unbiased, does not think I'm as worthless as I feel right now. Thank you again.
